name: 35745-structuredreasoning-gptoss20b-1gpu
hardware: 1x H100 80GB HBM3 (one GPU of an a3 node, --gres=gpu:1).
parallelism: TP=1, PP=1, DP=1. One vLLM engine, no model sharding.
architecture: GptOssForCausalLM MoE, 21B total / ~3.6B active per token, 24 layers, 32 experts (4 active), GQA 64 query / 8 KV heads, alternating 128-token sliding and full attention, MXFP4 MoE weights; all shapes in the checkpoint's own config.json.
load_profile: concurrent (closed loop), streams = 20, warmup 10%, cooldown 10%, bounded at 100 requests with a 1800 s safety cap, static seed 35745. A fixed number of callers all sending the same request size gives a flat resident batch, which is what makes a per-token latency readable; 16 to 32 streams all give the same picture.
workload: single-turn synthetic text: 1000 prompt tokens in and exactly 3000 out, both pinned min == max, with a JSON schema, a harmony chat template and three banned control tokens on every request. The schema (spec.backend.sampling_params.structured_outputs.json) is a one-property object, the smallest that is still a real constraint. The template (spec.backend.request_format: default-template) is the harmony template the checkpoint itself ships: it frames the synthetic text as a user message, closes it with <|end|> and opens the assistant turn, so the request is the one this model is built to answer. The banned tokens (sampling_params.bad_words: <|channel|>final, <|end|>, <|return|>) hold the response in one unbroken message for its declared length instead of one of whatever length the model chose.
purpose: A 20-billion-parameter analysis assistant writing 3000-token JSON reports from 1000-token prompts for 20 concurrent users on one GPU.
launch:
# Launch config for 35745-structuredreasoning-gptoss20b-1gpu. The engine is a source checkout,
# named by `configs/env.yaml`. Keep every key at column zero: an indented line is skipped.

model: openai/gpt-oss-20b

tensor-parallel-size: 1
pipeline-parallel-size: 1

# ~1100 prompt tokens (1000 synthetic plus the checkpoint's harmony wrapper) plus 3000 generated
# is ~4100 at the longest; 8192 clears it with room and keeps startup memory profiling small.
max-model-len: 8192

# BOTH LINES ARE LOAD-BEARING -- do not delete them as "the default". They set the resident batch
# this load profile is read against; left out, they fall through to whatever the scheduler's
# defaults are for the context the engine happens to be started in.
max-num-seqs: 1024
max-num-batched-tokens: 8192

# Both are the engine's own defaults at this commit, written down so a change of default cannot
# move them.
enable-prefix-caching: true
gpu-memory-utilization: 0.90
